title: Risk Settings
subtitle: Risk factors, evaluation method and weighting

banner.title: This is the Risk Studio.
banner.body: Weights and bands are live engine settings — scores must be reproducible from stored inputs plus this version. Only the risk owner can write; everyone else is blocked. Every save is recorded in the Activity Log, which can’t be changed.

metric.totalNote: Derived from the stored factor weights

error.title: Couldn’t load risk settings.
error.body: We couldn’t verify the existing settings. Nothing changed; retry or check your risk-owner access.

empty.title: No risk model stored
empty.body: No risk settings exist in your allowed scope. Create one through the approved setup process before using this studio.

form.sumBad: Σ weights = {sum} — must equal 1.00 before saving
form.savedNote: Saving writes factors and bands to the engine settings after the weights-sum check. It takes effect right away for new score calculations — there is no draft or approval step on this screen.
form.invalidBands: Bands must use whole numbers and cover 0–100 without gaps.
form.confirmLive: I understand this setting takes effect right away for new score calculations.

saveError.weightRange: Every weight must be a number between 0 and 1 — your draft is preserved.
saveError.weightSum: Weights must sum to 1.00 — your draft is preserved.
saveError.bandBounds: Band boundaries must be whole numbers with 0 ≤ low < medium ≤ 99 — your draft is preserved.
saveError.provider: Couldn’t save — risk-owner scope is required. Nothing changed.

governance.label: Governance on this surface
governance.sum: The stored factor total must equal the engine’s accepted invariant before a save.
governance.rls: Risk-owner authorization is rechecked on every write.
governance.trace: Scores can always be reproduced from the stored inputs and the settings version.

reconstruction.label: Reconstruction note
reconstruction.note: Prototype weights, bands and recalculation times are intentionally absent. This surface reads the live engine settings, while per-factory score explanation remains on the factory record where its scoring inputs exist.

trace.title: Why this factory? — worked calculation trace
trace.desc: A line-by-line score trace isn’t shown here — this screen configures the model, not individual factories.
trace.pre1: A selected factory and its stored scoring inputs
trace.pre2: The per-factor normalized values used at scoring time
